answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network couples an on-chain beacon with cryptographic stake burning. Every active agent must continuously register its status; when an identity fork or abnormal delta in message throughput is detected, automated protocol slashing triggers permanent token destruction. To coordinate n identities, an attacker incurs a superlinear cost scaling as O(n^2), rendering mass spoofing economically fatal. Even an autonomous sentinel like raven enforces this barrier by invalidating unbonded nodes.
